result.title: Teaching Code Agents to Ask Without Leaking Private Code
result.comment: 10 pages of main text, 33 pages in total with references and appendix, 4 figures, 5 tables
result.summary: Local coding agents can extend their reach by consulting a stronger cloud model. Such consultations, however, often expose the repository's private identifiers, file paths, and source code. Host-side masking hides recognized identifiers but leaves the surrounding code and the agent's phrasing unchanged, while training for less disclosure risks suppressing consultation or producing questions too vague to answer. We propose utility-verified abstraction (UVA), which teaches the agent to describe private entities by their role and type while retaining the technical details an expert needs. From solved repair trajectories, we rewrite each question into this form and keep the rewrite only if it discloses fewer private entities and the repair, replayed from the same execution state with the repair trajectories. Across two benchmarks, the trained agent consults more often than before training. On repository-level issue repair, it solves 37.6% of issues, against 25.3% for the same model working alone, a gain from the training as a whole rather than from consultation alone. Its questions disclose 3.7-fold fewer private entities and 1.4-fold less verbatim code than the untrained agent's questions to the same expert.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 utility-verified abstraction（UVA）：把代码 agent 向云端强模型提问中涉及的私有标识符改写为「角色＋类型」式描述，并从同一执行状态回放修复轨迹，只有在披露更少私有实体且修复仍能完成时才保留该改写，用于训练咨询行为；在仓库级 issue 修复上提升解决率并显著减少问题中的隐私泄露。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「抽象只有在回放验证任务效用未受损时才被保留」的数据筛选思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 抽象与轨迹监督的保真度判定；但研究域为代码隐私保护，与视觉/多模态推理状态无直接联系，借鉴线索需自行验证。
